lesson.subtitle: Lesson 14 -- The People I Work With
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ricardo Coutinho | Lesson 14 -- The People I Work With
lesson.grammar_point: adjective before the noun (word order): a friendly colleague / two new colleagues

listenings.text: Hi Ricardo, this is Amy. A quick message about tomorrow. There is a new colleague on the team. Her name is Karen, and she is from Chicago. She is young, but she is very experienced. She works with the dollar, like you. Her desk is near your desk, on the third floor. She is very friendly, so please say hello. See you tomorrow!

Hi, this is Paul again. A small piece of advice about people at work. In the United States, we describe a colleague with nice words. Friendly. Experienced. Funny. Very good with numbers. We do not talk about age at work. So, an experienced colleague is a nice thing to say. An old colleague is not nice. At work, one nice word is a small gift.

extra_audio.text: It is Monday, and I meet the Miami team. Paul is a tall and experienced manager. Amy is a young and friendly assistant. Diego is a new colleague from Colombia. Now I have two new colleagues!
